source.title: Information-theoretic generalization bounds for black-box learning algorithms
source.authors: Hrayr Harutyunyan; M. Raginsky; G. V. Steeg; A. Galstyan

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The experiments compare an information-based bound with measured generalization gaps in trained networks. This tests whether a measured property tracks the gap, but not the specific properties named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own f-CMI-bound and generalization-gap comparisons. Its discussion of random-label memorization and other prior findings cites earlier work; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates prediction-based information-theoretic bounds, not any property or intervention named in V1–V8. Its width comparison reports generalization gaps, without establishing interpolation or comparing held-out error beyond it. Random-label memorization is discussed through prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive prediction-based information-theoretic bounds that accommodate deterministic algorithms and are easier to estimate than weight-based alternatives. Experiments show useful agreement with generalization gaps in some settings, with substantial looseness early in training and an approximately threefold overestimate in the CIFAR-10 SGD experiment.
record.recipe_differences: Measures prediction-based f-CMI and compares it with the expected generalization gap; it does not test the interventions or properties specified by V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported f-CMI-bound/gap relationship varies with training stage: on MNIST with SGLD, the bound closely follows the gap after epoch 16, while it is large early despite a small gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated prediction-based f-CMI bounds are non-vacuous for deterministic MNIST training, with broadly similar results after fourfold widening. On CIFAR-10 the bound is about three times the measured gap. During SGLD training, relative tightness depends on training stage, and f-CMI can remain large despite a small gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prediction-based conditional mutual information can yield useful generalization-gap bounds for deterministic and stochastic neural-network training, although their tightness depends on task and training stage.

record.problems: Several experimental values are available only in figures; the paper notes that some experimental details are omitted from the main text and supplied in Appendix B. The CIFAR-10 ResNet-50 experiment uses one sample of Z̃ (k1 = 1), as stated in Table 4.

untested.parts: No paired natural-label and fixed-random-label training experiments or random-label held-out accuracy measurements.
No established interpolation threshold, zero-training-error comparison, or held-out-error trend beyond the width required to fit. The two-width gap comparison does not establish these.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison on the same workload; Adam and SGD appear in different experimental setups.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No dropout intervention or comparison with dropout removed.
No magnitude-aware weight sharpness measurements or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Prediction-based information and functional stability are different quantities.
No removal of highly memorized training examples and retraining against a random-removal control.

record.verdict_notes: None of the study's own results tests V1–V8, so no version verdicts are warranted. Comparisons of the proposed bound with other bounds belong under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-versus-random-label comparison.
A four-times-wider network is reported, but the paper does not report a width sweep of test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
The paper compares f-CMI bounds with gaps, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the listed norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: 4-layer convolutional neural network (CNN)
rows.operation_detail: Compared expected generalization gap with the f-CMI bound across training-set sizes.

conditions.value: ADAM with 0.001 learning rate and β1 = 0.9

rows.measure: Expected generalization gap and f-CMI bound
rows.uncertainty: The paper says the plotted error bars are standard deviations across k1 estimates; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The text says the bound is non-vacuous and not too far from the expected gap even with 75 examples, but gives no exact values.
rows.check: The measured f-CMI bound and generalization gap do not test any claim version. This is a result about the study's proposed bound.

rows.subject: 4-layer convolutional neural network (CNN), wider version
rows.operation_detail: Increased the width of all layers four times and compared the plotted gap and f-CMI bound.

conditions.value: four times the number of channels/neurons in each hidden layer

rows.measure: Expected generalization gap and f-CMI bound
rows.note: The authors state that the results remain largely unchanged; the figure supplies no textual numerical values.
rows.check: A largely unchanged generalization gap after widening does not establish unchanged test error or test V2. Neither zero training error nor widths relative to the interpolation threshold are reported. The introduction additionally states approximately 1% generalization gap for the 3M-parameter network with 4000 examples.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 pretrained on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared the expected generalization gap with the f-CMI bound.

conditions.value: SGD with 0.01 learning rate and 0.9 momentum
random horizontal flip and random 28x28 cropping

rows.measure: Expected generalization gap and f-CMI bound
rows.note: The paper says the bound is always approximately 3 times larger than the expected gap in this experiment.
rows.check: Change observed to cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. The 5% gap and 16% bound are correctly reported for n=20000, but Figure 1b also includes n=1000 and 5000; the roughly threefold bound-to-gap comparison spans those sizes. This evaluates the proposed bound, not a claim version.

rows.subject: 4-layer convolutional neural network (CNN)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked expected generalization gap, test error, f-CMI bound, and SGLD bound over training epochs.
rows.measure: Expected generalization gap, test error, f-CMI bound, and SGLD bound
rows.value: figure only; text says test accuracy plateaus after 16 epochs, f-CMI bound closely follows the gap at that time and afterwards, SGLD bound increases to very high values, and SGLD bound does better up to epoch 12.
rows.note: Text describes trends but provides no exact plotted values.
rows.check: Change observed to cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. The epoch-dependent comparison of f-CMI and SGLD bounds is accurately paraphrased, but evaluates bound performance rather than magnitude-aware sharpness or another named claim.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 pretrained on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared expected generalization gap with f-CMI and SGLD bounds during training.
rows.measure: Expected generalization gap, f-CMI bound, and SGLD bound
rows.value: after one epoch, SGLD bound approximately 0.45, generalization gap around 0.02, and f-CMI bound approximately 0.1
rows.note: The authors describe these values as approximate.
rows.check: Change observed to cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. The approximate one-epoch values are accurate; label 0.1 as the f-CMI bound rather than raw f-CMI. These are comparisons of bounds with the measured gap, not evidence for a named claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
